change.purpose: Operator request 2026-10-05: 'Om en kvant är fullbordad som t.ex. 1/1 eller 15/15 eller 1000/1000 eller vilket fullbordat exempel som helst så är det totalt onödigt att utföra analys av prompt och liknande om det inte tillför mervärde för sessionen eller Greenfield. Jag tänker att om kvanten är uppfylld så varför analysera och försöka skicka en prompt om ändå nästa steg är nästa GFW på tur?'
change.before: tickAnalyzing always ran the offscreen analysis (Nano observer, Hjalmar D2) on a captured answer and then decided the queue action. At a quantum boundary, or when the answer itself returned the slot to the queue (YIELD_TO_QUEUE, PAUSE_PROCESS, BACKGROUND_SLEEP), the planned follow-up prompt was never sent because the queue parked the slot and activated the next one (reproduced: tests/v1814-queue-boundary-no-analysis.test.mjs; on v1.8.13 every boundary check counts one analyzer call).
change.design: lib/queue-boundary.mjs (pure): skip analysis only when the queue-managed answer has a structured A2A control with status CONTINUE, no STOP_PROCESS/COMPLETE_MISSION, no NANO_TASK, and the queue action is certainly PARK_AND_SWITCH (quantum reached or explicit YIELD/PAUSE/SLEEP). background.js: another slot must take over (checked by applying the same park transition to a copy and selecting the next slot) and no operator instruction may be waiting; then, without a model call: runtime control with receipts, mission delegations, schedule gate, park with checkpoint (resume objective = the answer's own nextSuggestedAction, analysisEvidence.hjalmar = null, decision marked QUEUE_BOUNDARY_NO_ANALYSIS) and activation of the next slot. In every other case, and if the queue changes between the check and the park, the answer is analysed exactly as before.
change.implementation: lib/queue-boundary.mjs queueBoundaryAnalysisDecision, queueBoundaryControl, runtimeControlRequestsCompletion. background.js: capturedTargetResponse (deterministic A2A parse, now shared with runAnalysis), capturedResponseObservationEvidence and capturedProtocolEvidence (shared with tickAnalyzing), maybeParkAtQueueBoundaryWithoutAnalysis called in tickAnalyzing after the model/turn safety checks and before runAnalysis; audit QUEUE_BOUNDARY_ANALYSIS_SKIPPED and incident ANALYSIS_SKIPPED_AT_QUEUE_BOUNDARY.
change.unchanged: Model and turn safety checks before analysis, usage output recording, the analysis inside a quantum, DONE/BLOCKED/STOP handling, Nano tasks, operator instructions, the queue park itself (parkQueueMissionAfterAnalysis), quantum accounting, pauses, schedules, runtime-control rules (no priority above the operator's), the stale ladder and the slot hand-back of 1.8.13.

environment.kind: local Node harness with real background.js and mocked Chrome APIs; only the offscreen analyzer is mocked and counted; Chromium via Playwright for panel tools

reproductionBeforeChange.command: node --test tests/v1814-queue-boundary-no-analysis.test.mjs against the v1.8.13 tree (pure policy file copied in, not wired)
reproductionBeforeChange.result: 7/14: all 7 queue-boundary shortcut checks fail (v1.8.13 analyses every answer); the 6 'analysis still runs' controls and the pure policy test pass

claimBoundary.timeSaved: NOT_MEASURED (the 2026-10-05 export has no analysis durations)
claimBoundary.packageIntegrity: INTEGRITY.json binds packaged bytes; not a code-correctness proof

knownRemainingRisks: At a queue boundary Hjalmar no longer sees the answer: in 1.8.13 Hjalmar could on its own declare a GFW DONE or BLOCKED at the end of a quantum although the AI said CONTINUE; now the AI's own status decides (DONE/STOP still take the full path)
The parked slot resumes from the answer's own nextSuggestedAction instead of a Hjalmar-planned prompt; the resume prompt still tells the EIC to resume from Greenfield Works and fresh owner state
Everything listed for 1.8.13 (slot hand-back after the 30-minute reload, incident log size) still applies
